verdict.rationale: The keys provide hardware-backed authentication primitives that could gate sensitive actions: WebAuthn/FIDO2 authentication, OpenSSH connections to GitHub and Linux servers, PIV digital signatures, and on-device fingerprint matching that blocks use by anyone other than the authorized user. That makes a physical approval step plausible for automated workflows, such as SSH-based git operations an agent might trigger. Nothing in the evidence describes using the key to approve agent-initiated or automated actions, and the docs never explicitly say a touch is required per operation. Missing for 10: explicit per-operation touch/user-presence requirement documentation, any agent or automation approval workflow integration, guidance on gating non-login actions, independent or hands-on corroboration.
